## How this work is cited

Passages inside Le Deuxième Sexe are identified by volume and part or chapter. Two English versions are in circulation and they differ substantially: the 1953 Parshley edition cuts roughly a tenth of the text and simplifies the philosophical vocabulary, while the 2009 translation restores it. The archive records the volume, because the corpus's locators distinguish Vol. I from Vol. II.

## The work in Simone de Beauvoir’s thought

Simone de Beauvoir (1908–1986) was a French existentialist philosopher and novelist whose The Second Sex (1949) transformed feminist theory. A Normalienne, she partnered intellectually with Sartre while building an independent oeuvre on ethics, aging, and politics. [More on Simone de Beauvoir](https://www.philosophydef.com/thinkers/simone-de-beauvoir) .
